newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TELFER EXPECTS TOUGHER TASK FOR LIONS PACK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TELFER EXPECTS TOUGHER TASK FOR LIONS PACK.

text.p: British Lions forwards coach Jim Telfer said on Friday he expected a torrid time for his pack in Saturday's second test against South Africa.
The Lions won the first test 25-16. Their forwards were more mobile than the bigger South African pack but Telfer wants them to secure more quality possession in Durban.
"We definitely need more set-piece ball on Saturday and we need to use it constructively," Telfer said.

"And I would say it's going to be a far more daunting task for our scrum here in Durban. They (South Africa) are going to throw everything at us, the kitchen sink included. It's going to be very, very physical up front.
"Everyone is talking about the first 20 minutes being crucial and particularly intense. I think you'll find it'll be like that all the way through," he said.

Springbok coach Carel du Plessis has retained the scrum he fielded in the first test. "I expect them to raise their game by more than just one notch and I know the players are confident of doing that over the weekend," he said.

"We've also worked on the quality of our first, second and third phase possession and the platform you create there. I believe there will be a major improvement in that area of our game come Saturday."
